thread.title: Facebook faces more privacy questions as it announces record profit in earnings report - MarketWatch

author: Kari Paul
title: Facebook faces more privacy questions as it announces record profit in earnings report - MarketWatch
text:
Published: Jan 30, 2019 4:53 p.m. ET Share
The social media giant admitted to monitoring the online activity of children. AFP/Getty Images Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg introduces a new messenger platform on March 25, 2015.
By Kari Paul Reporter
As Facebook FB, +4.32% prepared to release its fourth-quarter earnings on Wednesday, consumer advocates renewed their call to the Federal Trade Commission to break up the world’s largest social media company.
In a complaint filed with the FTC on Tuesday, advocates asked the FTC to examine “significant revelations” in recent weeks regarding Facebook’s conduct. The letter was signed by more than a dozen activist groups, including Citizens Against Monopoly, Color of Change, and Democracy for America.
“As new controversies continue to pile up and consumer concern continues to grow, we would like to understand the general steps being taken in response to these matters,” the complaint said.
Facebook announced revenue of $16.91 billion in the fourth quarter of 2018 on Wednesday, an increase from $13.73 billion in the third quarter of 2018.
The FTC complaint that came ahead of the earnings was an update to a November letter the groups sent the FTC. It mentioned several scandals Facebook has been involved in since December, including revelations the platform allagedly shared user data with Amazon AMZN, +4.80% Spotify SPOT, +3.03% and Microsoft MSFT, +3.34% and another report that found Facebook allegedly tracks users’ location even if they disable all tracking features. Facebook did not respond to request for comment on the FTC complaint.
Since the FTC complaint was filed on Tuesday, even more privacy breaches have come to light. The company has allegedly been secretly paying users as young as 13 years old since 2016 to install an app called “Facebook Research,” a report from tech website TechCrunch found . This VPN reportedly lets the company monitor all user phone and web activity, according to TechCrunch. Apple AAPL, +6.83% removed the Facebook Research app from the app store following the story’s release.
Following a story that showed Facebook reportedly encouraged kids to run up bills on the app , this is another concern for parents of children on Facebook, said James P. Steyer, chief executive officer of Common Sense, a nonprofit organization devoted to improving media and entertainment for families.
“Once again, Facebook has been exposed for putting profits before people and for the second time in a week, it is kids who are being harmed,” he said. “Everyone is tired of Facebook saying sorry after being caught. There should be no questions for our leaders from Sacramento to Washington that this company needs to be regulated and held accountable.”
The groups writing to the FTC on Tuesday claim Facebook’s collection of data violates a 2012 agreement requiring it to disclose how much user data is obtained and how it is obtained. The advocates are calling for a fine of more than $22 million. The groups are also calling for Facebook to be broken up into smaller companies. The company currently owns Instagram and Whatsapp and is valued at more than $600 billion.
“At this point, Facebook needs to do a complete reset to regain user trust,” Theresa Payton, former White House chief information officer and founder/chief executive officer of cybersecurity consultancy Fortalice Solutions said. “This — and Apple’s FaceTime glitch this week — should serve as a huge warning to smart device users: the more you invite these devices and these social networks into your lives, the more at risk you are for breach and misuse of private information.”
